# Subject Merge Area Partition

## Quick Start

Create broad topic areas for one subject so later calls compare nearby candidates instead of the whole inventory. Use only the provided candidate cards.

## Decision Rules

- Partition by teachable neighborhood, not by exact duplicate identity.
- Prefer small, coherent neighborhoods over one large catch-all area.
- A full subject should usually have 15-25 areas when enough candidates exist.
- Put every input candidate ID in exactly one area.
- Keep mixed-language versions of the same topic in the same area.
- Do not decide final merges here. This step only creates neighborhoods.

## Output

Return one JSON object only:

```json
{
  "clusters": [
    {
      "id": "area_001",
      "label": "Short topic area",
      "rationale": "Why these candidates belong in the same broad neighborhood.",
      "candidate_ids": ["candidate-id"]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Self-Check

- Every input candidate ID appears exactly once.
- No area is a miscellaneous dump unless the input truly has isolated topics.
- Area labels describe topics, not final accepted concepts.
- No web search or external knowledge was used.

candidates.label: String Encoding and Decoding in Python
candidates.description: Understanding that strings in Python 3 are sequences of Unicode characters, and how to encode strings to bytes using specified encodings (e.g., UTF-8) and decode bytes back to strings, handling potential encoding errors.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução ao Processamento de Linguagem Natural

candidates.label: Natural Language Processing (NLP) Definition
candidates.description: NLP is a branch of AI that enables machines to read, understand, and derive meaning from human languages, combining linguistics and computer science.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução ao Processamento de Linguagem Natural

candidates.label: Everyday Applications of NLP
candidates.description: Common NLP applications include autocorrect for spelling and plagiarism checkers that scan for duplicate content.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução ao Processamento de Linguagem Natural

candidates.label: Text Preprocessing: Segmentation, Tokenization, and Stop Words
candidates.description: The initial NLP steps: breaking documents into sentences (segmentation), sentences into words (tokenization), and removing common stop words to focus on meaningful content.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução ao Processamento de Linguagem Natural

candidates.label: Word Normalization: Stemming and Lemmatization
candidates.description: Stemming reduces words to root forms by cutting suffixes (e.g., 'skipping' → 'skip'), while lemmatization uses dictionary-based analysis to find base forms (e.g., 'am', 'are', 'is' → 'be').
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução ao Processamento de Linguagem Natural

candidates.label: Linguistic Annotation: POS Tagging and Named Entity Recognition
candidates.description: POS tagging labels words with grammatical categories (noun, verb, etc.), while Named Entity Recognition identifies names, locations, and organizations in text.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução ao Processamento de Linguagem Natural

candidates.label: Machine Learning in NLP
candidates.description: After preprocessing, ML algorithms like Naive Bayes can be applied to tasks such as sentiment analysis, learning patterns from labeled data.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução ao Processamento de Linguagem Natural

candidates.label: NLP Definition and Suitability Criteria
candidates.description: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a branch of artificial intelligence that uses machine learning to process and interpret texts and data.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Expressões Regulares: Definição e Metacaracteres Básicos
candidates.description: Introduz expressões regulares como método para busca de padrões em textos e apresenta o conceito de metacaracteres, que são símbolos com significados especiais.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Metacaracteres Representantes: Ponto, Lista e Lista Negada
candidates.description: Descreve os metacaracteres representantes: ponto (.) que representa qualquer caractere, lista ([...]) que busca um dos caracteres listados e lista negada ([^...]) que busca caracteres que não estão na lista.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Metacaracteres Quantificadores
candidates.description: Apresenta os quantificadores: asterisco (*) para zero ou mais, opcional (?) para zero ou uma, mais (+) para uma ou mais e chaves ({x,y}) para um número específico de repetições, com exemplos usando classes de caracteres.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Âncoras: Circunflexo e Cifrão
candidates.description: Explica que o circunflexo (^) ancora a busca no início da linha/string e o cifrão ($) no final, destacando que ^ dentro de colchetes tem função de negação.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Alternação e Agrupamento
candidates.description: Mostra o uso do pipe (|) para alternância (OU) e dos parênteses ( ) para agrupar partes da regex, permitindo construir padrões com múltiplas opções.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Escapando Metacaracteres
candidates.description: Ensina que a contrabarra (\) é usada para tratar metacaracteres como literais, por exemplo, \.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Classes de Caracteres por Atalho
candidates.description: Apresenta os atalhos \d (dígito), \w (alfanumérico), \s (espaçamento) e suas negações \D, \W, \S, que simplificam a construção de padrões comuns.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Métodos Básicos do Módulo re do Python
candidates.description: Explora os métodos principais do módulo re do Python: match(), search(), findall() para busca de padrões, e split(), sub(), group() para manipulação de strings.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Aplicações Práticas de Regex
candidates.description: Ilustra casos reais de uso de expressões regulares: extração de e-mails, números de telefone, divisão de frases, detecção de acrônimos e validação de formatos como datas e IPs.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Similaridade Léxica
candidates.description: Define similaridade léxica como a medida de sobreposição de palavras ou caracteres entre dois fragmentos de texto, sem considerar significado, e discute os níveis de granularidade (caractere, palavra, frase).
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Distância de Edição Mínima e Levenshtein
candidates.description: Apresenta a distância de edição mínima como o número mínimo de operações (inserção, deleção, substituição) para transformar uma string em outra, e a variante Levenshtein onde a substituição custa 2.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Similaridade de Jaccard
candidates.description: Mede a similaridade entre dois conjuntos calculando a interseção dividida pela união, resultando em um valor entre 0 e 1, com exemplos em Python.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Similaridade de Cosseno
candidates.description: Calcula a similaridade entre dois vetores de frequência de palavras usando o cosseno do ângulo entre eles, com implementação em Python.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: N-grams para Predição de Texto
candidates.description: Define n-grams como sequências contíguas de n itens de um texto, usados em modelos de linguagem para prever a próxima palavra baseando-se em probabilidades.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Classificação de Algoritmos de Similaridade de Strings
candidates.description: Categoriza os algoritmos de similaridade em baseados em caracteres (ex.: Levenshtein) e baseados em termos (ex.: cosseno, Jaccard), indicando quando cada um é mais adequado.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Aplicações de Similaridade Textual
candidates.description: Lista e exemplifica aplicações reais de medidas de similaridade: sistemas de busca, recomendação, correção ortográfica, autocomplete, sumarização e detecção de duplicatas.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Similaridade Semântica e Diferenciação da Léxica
candidates.description: Define similaridade semântica como a que considera o significado das palavras em contexto, contrastando com a léxica, e fornece exemplos como 'carro' e 'automóvel'.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Abordagens para Similaridade Semântica: Baseadas em Conhecimento e Corpus
candidates.description: Descreve as duas principais abordagens para calcular similaridade semântica: baseada em corpus (grandes bases de texto) e baseada em conhecimento (redes semânticas como WordNet).
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: WordNet e Relações Semânticas
candidates.description: Apresenta a WordNet como um banco de dados lexical que organiza palavras em synsets e inclui relações semânticas como sinonímia, antonímia, meronímia, holonímia, hiponímia, hiperonímia, homonímia e polissemia.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Path Similarity e Lowest Common Subsumer (LCS)
candidates.description: Explica a similaridade de caminho (Path Similarity) como 1/(distância + 1) em uma taxonomia, e o LCS como o ancestral comum mais específico, ambos usando a WordNet.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Acesso à WordNet com NLTK (Inglês e Português)
candidates.description: Demonstra como acessar a WordNet em Python usando a biblioteca NLTK, incluindo suporte para português via Open Multilingual Wordnet (lang='por'), embora as definições estejam em inglês.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Aplicações de PLN (Visão Geral)
candidates.description: Lista e descreve aplicações de PLN: informação, tradução automática, sistemas de recomendação, smart replies, reconhecimento de voz, análise de sentimento, Q&A, extração de informação, sumarização, classificação, modelagem de tópicos, OCR, NER e geração de linguagem natural.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Ferramentas Google Cloud NLP
candidates.description: Apresenta as ferramentas do Google Cloud para PLN: API Natural Language, AutoML Natural Language, Dialogflow e Document AI, explicando suas funções e diferenças.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Desafios do PLN: Segmentação, Contexto e Semântica
candidates.description: Aborda desafios fundamentais do PLN: segmentação de texto, análise de contexto, extração de significado semântico e ambiguidade.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Desafios do PLN: Ortografia, Neologismos e Figuras de Linguagem
candidates.description: Cobre desafios relacionados a erros ortográficos, neologismos, figuras de linguagem e abreviações, que exigem tratamento especial em sistemas de PLN.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Desafios do PLN: Correferência, Negação e Recursos Limitados
candidates.description: Discute desafios de correferência, negação e especulação, e a limitação de recursos para língua portuguesa, incluindo a WordNet.Br.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Regex em JavaScript
candidates.description: Mostra como expressões regulares são criadas em JavaScript usando barras como delimitadores, com exemplo de negação de números.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: scikit-learn: Visão Geral e Algoritmos de Classificação, Regressão e Clustering
candidates.description: Apresenta a biblioteca scikit-learn para machine learning em Python, incluindo classificação, regressão, clustering, seleção de modelos e pré-processamento.
candidates.lesson_title: Processamento de texto, métricas e técnicas

candidates.label: Bag-of-Words Model Definition
candidates.description: The bag-of-words (BOW) model is a text representation technique that converts documents into fixed-length vectors by counting word occurrences, disregarding grammar and word order.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Vocabulary Construction in Bag-of-Words
candidates.description: The vocabulary is the set of all unique words across the document corpus.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: BOW Vectorization Process
candidates.description: The BOW vectorization process consists of determining the vocabulary (collecting unique words) and then counting the occurrences of each vocabulary word in each document to produce a count vector.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Loss of Word Order and Context in BOW
candidates.description: BOW discards the order of words, meaning it cannot capture syntax or semantics that depend on word sequence.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Implementing BOW with Keras Tokenizer
candidates.description: In Python, the Keras Tokenizer class can be used to implement BOW.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Applications and Strengths of BOW
candidates.description: Despite its simplicity, BOW is effective for tasks like text classification and profanity detection.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Text Preprocessing: Tokenization and Stopword Removal
candidates.description: Tokenization splits text into individual words (tokens).
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Sparse Vectors Problem
candidates.description: When the vocabulary is large, BOW vectors become mostly zeros (sparse), leading to high memory usage and computational inefficiency.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Implementing BOW from Scratch in Python
candidates.description: BOW can be implemented manually by writing functions to tokenize, remove stopwords, build a vocabulary, and generate count vectors using basic Python and NumPy.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Using Scikit-learn's CountVectorizer for BOW
candidates.description: Scikit-learn's CountVectorizer offers a ready-to-use BOW implementation with parameters for preprocessing, tokenization, n-grams, and more, outputting a term-document matrix.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: N-gram Extension to Bag-of-Words
candidates.description: BOW can be extended to n-grams (e.g., bigrams) where tokens are sequences of n consecutive words, partially capturing word order.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Why Text Needs to Be Converted to Numbers for Machine Learning
candidates.description: Machine learning algorithms require numerical input (matrices).
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Binary Bag-of-Words Encoding
candidates.description: In binary BOW, a sentence is represented by a binary vector where each dimension indicates the presence (1) or absence (0) of a vocabulary word, rather than its count.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Natural Language Challenges
candidates.description: Natural language is inherently structured yet free-form; the same meaning can be expressed in many ways, and similar words can convey different meanings, making NLP distinct from other data types.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Multi-label Encoding with Binary Vectors
candidates.description: In multi-label classification, labels are encoded as binary vectors where each index corresponds to a label, allowing a single example to have multiple 1s, unlike one-hot encoding for multi-class.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Sigmoid Activation for Multi-label Classification
candidates.description: For multi-label text classification with a bag-of-words model, the output layer should use sigmoid activation with binary cross-entropy loss, as it allows independent binary predictions per label, while softmax is for multi-class.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: HashVectorizer: Hashing-based Vectorization
candidates.description: Scikit-learn's HashVectorizer applies a hash function to map terms to numerical indices, saving memory but making it impossible to recover original feature names, unlike CountVectorizer.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: TfidfVectorizer: TF-IDF Weighting
candidates.description: Scikit-learn's TfidfVectorizer assigns weights to terms combining term frequency (TF) and inverse document frequency (IDF), giving higher importance to discriminative terms across the corpus, unlike simple count-based BoW.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Loading and exploring NLTK's Portuguese text corpora
candidates.description: How to import and access NLTK's built-in Portuguese corpora, including the examples module, Machado de Assis works, and the MacMorpho tagged corpus, to retrieve text, words, and tagged words.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Working with the Floresta treebank
candidates.description: How to access the Floresta Portuguese treebank, simplify its complex part-of-speech tags, and retrieve parsed syntactic trees.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Searching text with NLTK's built-in and regex methods
candidates.description: Using NLTK's concordance, similar, collocations, and findall with regex to locate words and analyze their contexts.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Tokenization with NLTK
candidates.description: Understanding tokenization as converting text into a list of words and punctuation, and using nltk.word_tokenize for better handling of contractions than simple regex splitting.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Analyzing tokenized text with NLTK and Python
candidates.description: Performing basic text analysis operations on tokenized lists, including extracting unique vocabulary, filtering/transforming tokens with list comprehensions, computing frequency distributions, and finding n-grams containing a target word.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Handling Portuguese text encoding (ISO 8859-1)
candidates.description: Awareness that many Portuguese text resources use ISO 8859-1 encoding and how to decode such text in Python when reading files.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Implementing a custom concordance tool
candidates.description: Writing a Python function that searches for a word in a list of sentences and prints it with surrounding context, mimicking NLTK's concordance.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Stemming with Porter Stemmer in NLTK
candidates.description: Using the Porter Stemmer algorithm to reduce words to their stems through rule-based suffix stripping.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Snowball Stemmer for multilingual stemming
candidates.description: Snowball Stemmer is a stemming algorithm supporting multiple languages, often more accurate than Porter Stemmer.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Lemmatization with WordNetLemmatizer
candidates.description: WordNetLemmatizer reduces words to dictionary form using WordNet.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Processing text and exploring documents, tokens, and spans in spaCy
candidates.description: Use spacy.blank to create a pipeline and process text into a Doc.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Using lexical attributes for pattern detection
candidates.description: Token attributes like `like_num` can identify numeric tokens.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Loading and understanding pre-trained spaCy models
candidates.description: Load pre-trained pipelines with spacy.load.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Predicting part-of-speech tags and dependencies
candidates.description: After processing text with a trained pipeline, each token has a .pos_ (coarse POS tag) and .dep_ (dependency label).
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Named entity recognition and manual correction
candidates.description: Trained pipelines identify named entities (doc.ents).
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Rule-based matching with Matcher
candidates.description: Use the Matcher class to define token-based patterns with attributes and operators for finding sequences in text.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Introduction to Natural Language Processing (NLP)
candidates.description: NLP is the field of making computers understand natural language, relying on statistical approximations; applications include information extraction and chatbots.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Overview of spaCy as a production-ready NLP library
candidates.description: spaCy is an open-source MIT-licensed NLP library, maintained by Explosion.ai, supporting 73 languages and focused on production with pre-trained models.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Contêineres spaCy: Doc, Token e Span
candidates.description: No spaCy, um Doc representa o documento inteiro processado, contendo uma sequência de objetos Token.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Atributos de tokens no spaCy: text, shape_ e is_alpha
candidates.description: Cada token possui atributos como .text, .shape_ e .is_alpha que descrevem sua forma e tipo, permitindo filtrar ou identificar padrões no texto.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: POS tagging – classificação gramatical dos tokens
candidates.description: POS tagging atribui a cada token uma classe gramatical (ex.: substantivo, verbo).
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Lematização – redução à forma canônica
candidates.description: Lematização transforma palavras flexionadas em sua forma base (ex.: 'faz' → 'fazer').
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Análise de dependências sintáticas (dep_)
candidates.description: A análise de dependências atribui a cada token um rótulo .dep_ indicando sua função sintática (ex.: nsubj para sujeito, obj para objeto).
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Reconhecimento de Entidades Nomeadas (NER) no spaCy
candidates.description: NER identifica entidades como pessoas, organizações, locais no texto.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Naive Bayes Classifier Core
candidates.description: Naive Bayes is a probabilistic classifier that applies Bayes' theorem with the naive assumption of feature independence given the class.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Probability Foundations for Naive Bayes
candidates.description: Foundational probability concepts: basic probability, conditional probability P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B), and Bayes theorem P(B|A) = P(A|B)P(B)/P(A) with posterior, likelihood, prior, and evidence.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Feature Independence Assumption and Multicollinearity
candidates.description: Naive Bayes assumes features are independent given the class (the 'naive' assumption).
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Naive Bayes Variants: Bernoulli, Multinomial, Gaussian
candidates.description: Three main variants: Bernoulli for binary features, Multinomial for discrete counts (especially text), and Gaussian for continuous features assuming a normal distribution.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Zero Frequency Error and Laplace Smoothing
candidates.description: Zero frequency error occurs when a test feature value was not seen during training, causing zero posterior probability.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Practical Aspects of Naive Bayes: Applications, Advantages, and Usage
candidates.description: Naive Bayes is used in text classification, sentiment analysis, recommendation, and real-time prediction.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Improving Naive Bayes Performance
candidates.description: Techniques include removing correlated features, feature engineering, domain knowledge, using probabilistic features, Laplace smoothing, and the log-trick for numerical stability: argmax (log prior + Σ log P(xᵢ|y)).
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Gaussian Naive Bayes: Prior, Likelihood, and PDF
candidates.description: In Gaussian Naive Bayes, the prior P(y) is the class frequency.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Naive Bayes Training and Prediction Procedure
candidates.description: Training: compute per-class means, variances, and prior probabilities.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Implementing Naive Bayes in Python
candidates.description: The classifier is implemented as a Python class with fit() and predict() methods, using NumPy arrays, storing learned parameters as attributes.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Sentiment Analysis: Definition and Supervised Learning
candidates.description: Sentiment analysis classifies text as positive or negative based on sentiment-bearing words.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Bag-of-Words Representation
candidates.description: The bag-of-words model represents text as a vector of word frequencies, ignoring word order.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Derivation of Naive Bayes Decision Rule
candidates.description: The step-by-step derivation from Bayes theorem to the final classification formula: select class c that maximizes P(c) * ∏ P(word|c).
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Naive Bayes Training: Prior and Likelihood Computation
candidates.description: How to compute prior class probabilities P(c) = Nc/N and word likelihoods P(word|c) as relative frequency in class c.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Laplace Smoothing in Naive Bayes
candidates.description: Adding a constant (usually 1) to all word counts to avoid zero probabilities for unseen words, using the formula (count + 1) / (total words + vocabulary size).
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Logarithmic Transformation for Numerical Stability
candidates.description: Using the log of the Naive Bayes product to convert it into a sum, preventing underflow from multiplying many small probabilities.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Stop Words Removal
candidates.description: Filtering out common words (e.g., 'the', 'is') that carry little semantic value, using predefined lists such as NLTK's stopwords.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Basic Text Cleaning
candidates.description: Lowercasing text and removing HTML tags, special characters, and punctuation to reduce noise and ensure uniformity.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Stemming
candidates.description: Reducing words to their root form (e.g., 'running' → 'run') to consolidate terms, using algorithms like SnowballStemmer from NLTK.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Binary Multinomial Naive Bayes
candidates.description: A variant that uses binary features (word presence/absence) instead of word counts, emphasizing occurrence over frequency.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Word-level Tokenization
candidates.description: Splitting raw text into individual words (tokens) as the first step of NLP pipelines, often using functions like d2l.tokenize.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Vocabulary Construction and Out-of-Vocabulary Handling
candidates.description: Building a vocabulary from training tokens with a minimum frequency filter, and ignoring unknown words during testing to avoid errors.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Natural Language Processing (NLP) Definition
candidates.description: NLP is a subfield of AI focused on enabling computers to process and analyze human language, applied to tasks like text classification and sentiment analysis.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Bag of Words with CountVectorizer
candidates.description: Converting preprocessed text into a numerical matrix of token counts using scikit-learn's CountVectorizer, often with max_features to limit vocabulary size.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Fundamentos do Naive Bayes
candidates.description: Compreensão do teorema de Bayes, da suposição de independência ingênua, e como eles formam a base do classificador Naive Bayes para classificação de texto.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Aplicação do Multinomial Naive Bayes em scikit-learn
candidates.description: Implementação prática do classificador MultinomialNB para análise de sentimento ou detecção de spam, incluindo preparação dos dados e treinamento.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Divisão treino-teste para avaliação de modelos
candidates.description: Particionamento dos dados em conjuntos de treino e teste para avaliar a generalização do modelo e detectar overfitting.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Métricas de avaliação para classificação
candidates.description: Métricas derivadas da matriz de confusão: acurácia, precisão, recall, F1-score, para avaliar o desempenho de classificadores binários.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Ajuste de hiperparâmetros com GridSearchCV
candidates.description: Busca exaustiva dos melhores hiperparâmetros usando validação cruzada para otimizar o desempenho do classificador Naive Bayes.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Distribuição de classes desbalanceada
candidates.description: Identificação de conjuntos de dados com desproporção entre classes e compreensão de seu impacto na classificação.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Analogias com Vetores de Palavras (Word2Vec)
candidates.description: Word2Vec produz embeddings densos que permitem realizar analogias através de operações aritméticas, como 'rei - homem + mulher ≈ rainha', evidenciando que as relações semânticas são codificadas como direções no espaço vetorial.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Incorporação 2D Simplificada para Visualizar Similaridade
candidates.description: É possível construir word embeddings bidimensionais atribuindo manualmente pontuações (ex.: fofura e tamanho) para animais, de modo que palavras similares fiquem próximas no espaço vetorial, ilustrando o princípio da similaridade semântica por proximidade espacial.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Alta Dimensionalidade dos Embeddings Reais e Redução de Dimensionalidade
candidates.description: Modelos word2vec reais usam centenas de dimensões (100-300) para capturar relações semânticas complexas, impossibilitando visualização direta; técnicas como t-SNE ou PCA são necessárias para projetar em 2D.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Hipótese Distributiva
candidates.description: A hipótese distributiva afirma que palavras que aparecem em contextos similares tendem a ter significados similares, fundamentando a representação vetorial semântica.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Similaridade por Cosseno entre Vetores de Palavras
candidates.description: A similaridade de cosseno mede o ângulo entre dois vetores para quantificar proximidade semântica, sendo preferida ao produto escalar por normalizar a magnitude e evitar viés de palavras frequentes.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Arquiteturas do Word2Vec: CBOW e Skip-Gram
candidates.description: Word2Vec possui duas arquiteturas principais: CBOW (Continuous Bag-of-Words) prevê a palavra central a partir do contexto, enquanto Skip-Gram prevê o contexto a partir da palavra central.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Treinamento do Word2Vec e Amostragem Negativa
candidates.description: O treinamento do Word2Vec maximiza a probabilidade de pares palavra-contexto usando uma função softmax; para reduzir custo, a amostragem negativa gera exemplos negativos, otimizando o cálculo.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Comparação entre Word2Vec, GloVe e fastText
candidates.description: Word2Vec foca em contexto local, GloVe utiliza estatísticas globais de co-ocorrência, e fastText usa subword n-grams para representar palavras desconhecidas, oferecendo diferentes trade-offs.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: BERT: Embeddings Bidirecionais com Transformers
candidates.description: BERT é um modelo de embedding contextual que utiliza transformers bidirecionais para considerar o contexto à esquerda e à direita, gerando representações dinâmicas e ricas.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Pré-processamento para Word Embeddings
candidates.description: Etapas comuns de pré-processamento incluem conversão para minúsculas, remoção de pontuações e stop words, e tokenização, com o objetivo de uniformizar o texto antes da vetorização.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Limitações do TF-IDF
candidates.description: O TF-IDF pondera frequência de termos pela inversa da frequência nos documentos, mas produz vetores esparsos de alta dimensionalidade que não capturam semântica complexa.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Word Embeddings: Definição e Motivação
candidates.description: Word embeddings são representações densas de palavras em um espaço vetorial, capturando significado semântico e contrastando com representações esparsas como bag-of-words.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Documento, Corpus e Streaming no Gensim
candidates.description: No Gensim, um documento é uma sequência de texto (str), um corpus é uma coleção de documentos para treinamento não supervisionado, e o streaming permite processar grandes corpora sem carregar tudo em memória.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Vetores Esparsos no Gensim
candidates.description: Vetores no Gensim representam documentos como bag-of-words esparsas, onde cada feature é um contador de palavra, omitindo zeros para economia de memória.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Modelos no Gensim como Transformações
candidates.description: Um modelo no Gensim aprende uma transformação entre espaços vetoriais (ex.: BOW para TF-IDF) a partir de um corpus de treinamento e pode ser aplicado a novos documentos.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Dicionário Gensim e Vetorização com doc2bow
candidates.description: A classe Dictionary mapeia cada palavra do corpus para um ID inteiro único, e o método doc2bow converte documentos tokenizados em vetores bag-of-words.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Modelo TF-IDF no Gensim
candidates.description: O modelo TF-IDF transforma vetores bag-of-words ponderando as frequências dos termos pela inversa da frequência nos documentos, dando menos peso a palavras comuns e mais a palavras raras.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: Similarity Queries with Gensim
candidates.description: After transforming a corpus with a model (e.g., TF-IDF), Gensim can compute similarity scores between a query document and all documents in the corpus, enabling search and clustering.
candidates.lesson_title: Vetores multidimensionais: Word2Vec e Gensim

candidates.label: McCulloch-Pitts neuron model
candidates.description: The first computational model of a neuron proposed by McCulloch and Pitts in 1943, representing neurons as simple electrical circuits with binary outputs.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Hebbian learning
candidates.description: The principle that neural connections are strengthened when the pre- and post-synaptic neurons fire together, introduced by Donald Hebb in 1949 and later formalized as a learning rule.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Perceptron
candidates.description: A single-layer neural network model by Frank Rosenblatt (1958) that computes a weighted sum of inputs, subtracts a threshold, and outputs a binary class; it defines a linear decision boundary.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: ADALINE and MADALINE
candidates.description: Early adaptive linear neural networks (ADALINE, MADALINE) developed by Widrow and Hoff (1959) that used adaptive linear elements; MADALINE was the first neural network applied to a real-world problem (echo cancellation).
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Minsky & Papert critique and the AI winter
candidates.description: The 1969 book 'Perceptrons' by Minsky and Papert proved the limitations of single-layer perceptrons, leading to a halt in neural network funding and research throughout the 1970s.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Hopfield networks and the revival of neural network research
candidates.description: John Hopfield's 1982 paper and the US-Japan Conference on Cooperative Competitive Neural Networks rekindled interest and funding in neural networks, ending the AI winter.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
candidates.description: A specialized recurrent neural network architecture using gated memory cells (forget, input, output gates) to learn long-term dependencies and mitigate the vanishing gradient problem; introduced by Hochreiter and Schmidhuber in 1997.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Backpropagation
candidates.description: The core learning algorithm for neural networks that computes the gradient of the loss function with respect to weights using the chain rule and updates weights in the opposite direction to minimize error.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Feedforward neural network architecture
candidates.description: A neural network organized into sequential layers (input, hidden, output) where connections flow only forward without cycles; each neuron computes a weighted sum plus bias followed by an activation function.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) basics
candidates.description: A neural network architecture with feedback connections that pass information from one time step to the next, creating an internal memory suitable for sequential data.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Autoencoder
candidates.description: An unsupervised neural network that compresses input into a lower-dimensional representation (encoding) and reconstructs the original input (decoding), useful for dimensionality reduction and feature learning.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)
candidates.description: A framework where a generator network creates synthetic data and a discriminator network tries to distinguish it from real data; adversarial training improves both.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Activation Functions
candidates.description: Non-linear activation functions (sigmoid, tanh, ReLU, step, softmax) applied to neuron outputs introduce non-linearity into the network, enabling learning of complex patterns.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Loss Functions
candidates.description: Loss functions quantify the prediction error during training, guiding weight updates.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Convolutional Neural Networks
candidates.description: CNNs are architectures for grid-structured data (e.g., images) that use convolutional layers to detect spatial features, pooling layers to reduce dimensionality, and fully-connected layers for classification.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Deep Residual Networks
candidates.description: Deep Residual Networks (DRNs) use skip connections (residual blocks) to allow gradients to flow through very deep architectures, mitigating the vanishing gradient problem and enabling training of networks like ResNet.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Keras for Neural Networks
candidates.description: Keras is a high-level TensorFlow API that simplifies neural network construction.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Overfitting and Regularization
candidates.description: Overfitting occurs when a model learns training noise and fails to generalize; underfitting is the opposite.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Linear Algebra Foundations
candidates.description: Neural network computations rely on linear vector spaces, inner products, norms, and linear transformations.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Gradient Descent Optimization
candidates.description: Gradient descent minimizes the loss by iteratively updating parameters: w = w - η * ∇J.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Neural Network Training Implementation
candidates.description: Training involves: forward propagation to compute outputs; random weight initialization to break symmetry; a loop over epochs performing forward, cost, backward, and update steps; layer dimensions determine parameter shapes; caches store intermediate values for backprop.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Perceptron and Its Limitations
candidates.description: The perceptron is a single neuron with step activation: output = step(∑ w_i x_i + b).
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Data Preparation for Neural Networks
candidates.description: Non-numeric inputs must be encoded (e.g., binary encoding, one-hot encoding) for neural networks.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Divisão Treino/Teste
candidates.description: A técnica de separar dados em conjuntos de treino e teste para avaliar a generalização de modelos.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Implementação Manual vs Bibliotecas
candidates.description: Comparação entre implementar um perceptron do zero e usar scikit-learn, destacando a redução de código e complexidade.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Acurácia
candidates.description: Métrica de avaliação que calcula a proporção de predições corretas, variando de 0 a 1.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Perceptron Multicamadas
candidates.description: Introdução ao perceptron multicamadas como uma extensão para resolver problemas não-linearmente separáveis.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: Rede Neural Artificial
candidates.description: Uma rede neural artificial é um modelo preditivo inspirado no cérebro, composto por neurônios artificiais conectados que realizam cálculos ponderados sobre as entradas e produzem saídas através de funções de ativação.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução a Rede Neural

candidates.label: What is Keras?
candidates.description: Keras is a high-level deep learning API, available standalone and integrated into TensorFlow (tf.keras), designed to simplify the implementation of neural networks.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Keras Backend Flexibility
candidates.description: Keras supports multiple backend computation engines such as TensorFlow, Theano, PlaidML, MXNet, and CNTK, with TensorFlow adopting Keras as its official high-level API.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Keras Model Types
candidates.description: Keras provides two primary ways to define a neural network: the Sequential model for linear stacks of layers, and the Functional API for complex architectures with shared layers or multiple inputs/outputs.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Building a Sequential Model with Dense Layers
candidates.description: A simple feedforward neural network in Keras can be constructed using the Sequential model and stacking Dense layers with specified units and activation functions (e.g., ReLU for hidden layers, softmax for the output layer).
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Compiling a Keras Model
candidates.description: Before training, a Keras model must be compiled using model.compile() to configure the learning process by specifying a loss function (e.g., categorical_crossentropy), an optimizer (e.g., rmsprop), and metrics (e.g., accuracy).
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Training a Keras Model with fit()
candidates.description: The model.fit() method trains the compiled model on training data, with key hyperparameters such as epochs (number of passes over the dataset) and batch_size (samples per gradient update).
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Evaluating a Keras Model on Test Data
candidates.description: After training, model.evaluate() computes the loss and any specified metrics (e.g., accuracy) on a held‑out test set, providing an unbiased estimate of model performance.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Making Predictions with Keras Models
candidates.description: Trained Keras models can generate predictions on new data using model.predict() to obtain probability distributions, and np.argmax() (or model.predict_classes()) to get the predicted class labels.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Normalizing Pixel Values for Neural Networks
candidates.description: To improve training stability, pixel values of images (originally 0‑255) should be normalized to the [0,1] range by dividing by 255.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Reshaping and Flattening Image Data for Dense Layers
candidates.description: Since Dense layers expect 1D input, 2D image arrays must be reshaped into 1D vectors, either manually with .reshape() or by inserting a Flatten layer as the first layer in the model.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: One‑Hot Encoding for Categorical Labels
candidates.description: For multi‑class classification, integer labels must be converted to one‑hot encoded vectors using tf.keras.utils.to_categorical() so that the model output can be compared against a probability distribution.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Inspecting a Keras Model
candidates.description: Keras provides several methods to inspect a model's architecture and weights, including summary(), get_config(), and get_weights().
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Saving and reloading Keras models
candidates.description: How to persist a trained Keras model to an HDF5 file using model.save() and restore it with load_model() from tensorflow.keras.models.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Fine-tuning with custom optimizer parameters
candidates.description: How to customize the optimizer by instantiating it with specific learning rate and decay values (e.g., RMSprop(lr=0.0001, decay=1e-6)) and compiling the model with it.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Fine-tuning with Early Stopping
candidates.description: How to use the EarlyStopping callback to stop training when a monitored metric (e.g., validation loss) stops improving after a given patience, preventing overfitting.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Keras model building workflow
candidates.description: The sequential pipeline for building a neural network in Keras: import modules, create a Sequential model, add layers, compile with optimizer and loss, fit on data, and make predictions.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Loading built-in Keras datasets
candidates.description: How to load standard datasets like MNIST, CIFAR-10, Boston Housing, and IMDb directly from tensorflow.keras.datasets, including splitting into training and test sets.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: MNIST dataset characteristics
candidates.description: The MNIST dataset consists of 28x28 grayscale images of handwritten digits 0-9, with 60,000 training and 10,000 test samples.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Inspecting data shape and labels
candidates.description: After loading data, how to inspect array shapes (e.g., train_images.shape) and visualize samples using matplotlib to verify the data before modeling.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Sequence padding for RNNs
candidates.description: How to pad variable-length sequences to a fixed length using tensorflow.keras.preprocessing.sequence.pad_sequences, with specification of maxlen, to prepare data for recurrent neural networks.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Train/test split with sklearn
candidates.description: How to partition a dataset into training and test subsets using sklearn.model_selection.train_test_split, controlling proportions with test_size and reproducibility with random_state.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Standardization with StandardScaler
candidates.description: How to standardize features by scaling them to have zero mean and unit variance using StandardScaler from sklearn.preprocessing, fitting on training data and transforming both train and test sets.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Building an MLP for binary classification
candidates.description: Constructing a Sequential model with Dense layers for binary classification: relu activation for hidden layers and sigmoid for the output layer.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Building an MLP for multi-class classification with Dropout
candidates.description: Stacking Dense layers with relu activation, interspersed with Dropout for regularization, and ending with a softmax output layer for multi-class classification.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Building an MLP for regression
candidates.description: Construct a regression neural network using Dense layers without activation on the output to predict continuous values.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Building a CNN in Keras
candidates.description: Construct a convolutional neural network using Conv2D, Activation, MaxPooling2D, Dropout, Flatten, and Dense layers.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Building an RNN with LSTM
candidates.description: Create a recurrent neural network by adding an Embedding layer and an LSTM layer with dropout, followed by a Dense output for binary classification.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Loading external data from a URL with NumPy
candidates.description: Use urllib.request.urlopen and np.loadtxt to fetch a CSV dataset from a URL and split it into feature matrix and target vector.
candidates.lesson_title: Rede Neural com Keras (Tensorflow)

candidates.label: Distributional Hypothesis of Meaning
candidates.description: The distributional hypothesis states that words with similar meanings occur in similar contexts.
candidates.lesson_title: Word2Vec - Aplicação utilizando Redes Neurais

candidates.label: Word Vectors as Numerical Representations
candidates.description: Words can be encoded as vectors of numbers, where each dimension represents a semantic or descriptive feature such as authority, richness, or gender.
candidates.lesson_title: Word2Vec - Aplicação utilizando Redes Neurais

candidates.label: Vector Arithmetic for Semantic Analogies
candidates.description: Word vectors learned by Word2Vec support vector arithmetic that reflects semantic relationships, enabling analogy solving (e.g., 'king' - 'man' + 'woman' ≈ 'queen').
candidates.lesson_title: Word2Vec - Aplicação utilizando Redes Neurais

candidates.label: Semantic and Syntactic Relationships in Word2Vec Embeddings
candidates.description: Word2Vec embeddings capture a variety of linguistic relationships, including verb tenses, capital-country associations, and gender pairs, by encoding them as consistent vector offsets.
candidates.lesson_title: Word2Vec - Aplicação utilizando Redes Neurais

candidates.label: Similarity Measures for Word Vectors
candidates.description: Euclidean distance and cosine similarity are two metrics used to quantify the similarity between word vectors.
candidates.lesson_title: Word2Vec - Aplicação utilizando Redes Neurais

candidates.label: Training Data Generation for Word2Vec
candidates.description: How training samples are created for Word2Vec: using a sliding window to form context-target pairs, representing words with one-hot encoding, and the distinction between CBOW and Skip-gram architectures.
candidates.lesson_title: Word2Vec - Aplicação utilizando Redes Neurais

candidates.label: Word Embeddings as Neural Network Weights
candidates.description: In Word2Vec, the word embeddings are the learned weights connecting the one-hot input to the hidden layer (or hidden to output, depending on architecture).
candidates.lesson_title: Word2Vec - Aplicação utilizando Redes Neurais

candidates.label: Análise de Sentimentos
candidates.description: Técnicas para classificar a polaridade de textos, como positivo, negativo ou neutro.
candidates.lesson_title: Word2Vec - Aplicação utilizando Redes Neurais

candidates.label: Nearest Neighbor Retrieval using Word Vectors
candidates.description: Finding the most similar words or items in a vector space by computing distances (e.g., cosine similarity) to all candidates and selecting the closest ones.
candidates.lesson_title: Word2Vec - Aplicação utilizando Redes Neurais

candidates.label: Count-based Word Vector Construction and Dimensionality Reduction
candidates.description: Word vectors can be built by counting word co-occurrences in contexts from a corpus.
candidates.lesson_title: Word2Vec - Aplicação utilizando Redes Neurais

candidates.label: Using Pre-trained Word Embeddings
candidates.description: Several publicly available pre-trained word vectors, such as GloVe (300-dimensional) and Google's word2vec model, can be easily loaded via libraries like spaCy or gensim.downloader.
candidates.lesson_title: Word2Vec - Aplicação utilizando Redes Neurais

candidates.label: Sentence Similarity through Averaged Word Vectors
candidates.description: A sentence can be represented as the average of its word vectors.
candidates.lesson_title: Word2Vec - Aplicação utilizando Redes Neurais

candidates.label: Gensim Library and Text Preprocessing
candidates.description: Gensim is an open-source NLP library providing tools for text preprocessing and analysis.
candidates.lesson_title: Word2Vec - Aplicação utilizando Redes Neurais

candidates.label: Training Word2Vec Models with Gensim
candidates.description: Gensim's Word2Vec class trains word embeddings on preprocessed sentences.
candidates.lesson_title: Word2Vec - Aplicação utilizando Redes Neurais

candidates.label: Feature Extraction in NLP
candidates.description: The process of transforming cleaned text into numerical features that machine learning algorithms can process, a fundamental step in NLP pipelines.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Bag of Words (BoW)
candidates.description: A text representation that counts word occurrences in a document, ignoring order but preserving multiplicity, often forming a document-term matrix.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: TF-IDF
candidates.description: A weighting scheme that scales term frequency by the inverse of document frequency to highlight words that are important to a specific document within a corpus.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: One-hot Encoding
candidates.description: A sparse representation where each word is a vector of zeros with a single 1 at the index corresponding to the word in the vocabulary.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Word Embedding
candidates.description: Dense, low-dimensional vector representations of words that capture semantic similarities, enabling analogies through vector arithmetic.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Word2Vec
candidates.description: A shallow neural network model that learns word embeddings from large corpora using either the Continuous Bag of Words (CBOW) or skip-gram architecture.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
candidates.description: GloVe is an unsupervised learning algorithm for generating word embeddings by factorizing a word co-occurrence matrix, capturing global statistical information.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Implementing Feature Extraction in Python for NLP
candidates.description: Practical implementation of NLP feature extraction pipelines using Python libraries such as scikit-learn, NLTK, and spaCy, including loading text data and applying methods like CountVectorizer.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Comparing Word Embedding and Feature Extraction Approaches for NLP
candidates.description: Analyzing the differences between NLP systems built using pre-trained word embeddings (e.g., Word2Vec, GloVe) versus traditional feature extraction methods, including trade-offs in dimensionality, semantic capture, and model complexity.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Building a Python Web API to Serve NLP Models
candidates.description: Developing a Python-based web API to serve NLP models, using frameworks like Flask or FastAPI, including steps to wrap a model into a REST endpoint and considerations like latency and data serialization.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Creating a Basic Flask API Endpoint
candidates.description: Setting up a minimal Flask application by importing Flask, creating an instance, defining a route with @app.route to bind a view function that returns data (e.g., JSON), and running the app.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Handling Dynamic URL Parameters and URL Generation in Flask
candidates.description: Using Flask's variable rules to capture dynamic parts of a URL (e.g., <int:user_id>) and employing url_for() to generate URLs for view functions, promoting maintainable and flexible endpoint design.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: Defining API endpoints with HTTP methods in Flask
candidates.description: Specify allowed HTTP methods with the methods argument to @app.route; use request.method to branch, or use shortcut decorators @app.get/@app.post.
candidates.lesson_title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs

candidates.label: One-Hot Encoding
candidates.description: One-hot encoding represents each word as a sparse vector with a 1 at the vocabulary index and zeros elsewhere, resulting in high-dimensional, inefficient representations.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Count-Based Text Representations and Limitations
candidates.description: Bag-of-Words and TF-IDF represent text by counting words (or n-grams) and weighting them by importance.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Word Embeddings as Dense Vectors
candidates.description: Unlike sparse encodings, word embeddings are dense numerical vectors where each dimension captures latent features.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Semantic Similarity and Properties of Embedding Space
candidates.description: In a distributional framework, words are similar if they share similar contexts.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Training a Custom Embedding Layer
candidates.description: A neural network can include an embedding layer initialized randomly and trained end‑to‑end for a specific task, producing specialized word representations.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Word2vec: CBOW and Skip‑gram Architectures
candidates.description: Word2vec learns embeddings by training a shallow neural network on a prediction task: Continuous Bag‑of‑Words (CBOW) predicts a target word from context, while Skip‑gram predicts context words from a target word.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
candidates.description: GloVe improves on Word2vec by leveraging a word co‑occurrence matrix, training vectors such that their dot product approximates the log of co‑occurrence probability, thereby incorporating global corpus statistics.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: fastText: Subword Embeddings
candidates.description: fastText represents each word as the sum of its character n‑gram embeddings, allowing it to build vectors for out‑of‑vocabulary words and handle morphologically rich languages.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: ELMo: Contextualized Word Embeddings
candidates.description: ELMo uses a bidirectional LSTM to produce word vectors that depend on the entire input sentence, allowing the same word to have different representations in different contexts (e.g., homonyms).
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Using Pre‑trained Word Embeddings
candidates.description: Pre‑trained word vectors can be used in two ways: as static features (fixed during downstream training) or fine‑tuned (adjusted to the task).
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: TF-IDF Definition and Computation
candidates.description: TF-IDF is a statistical measure of word relevance in a document corpus, computed as the product of Term Frequency (TF) and Inverse Document Frequency (IDF).
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: TF-IDF Output: Document Vectors and Applications
candidates.description: After computing TF-IDF for all terms, each document is represented as a weighted term vector, where high weights indicate discriminative terms.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: TF-IDF Discriminative Power and Comparison with Bag of Words
candidates.description: TF-IDF assigns higher weights to terms that appear frequently in a specific document but rarely across the corpus, making them discriminative features.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Implementing TF-IDF with Scikit-learn: TfidfVectorizer and Preprocessing
candidates.description: In Python, TF-IDF can be computed using TfidfVectorizer from sklearn.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: NLP Vocabulary: Document, Body, Dictionary, Topic
candidates.description: In NLP, a document is a single data instance (e.g., a paragraph, tweet).
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA) Definition
candidates.description: LSA is an unsupervised NLP technique that discovers latent topics in a corpus by applying dimensionality reduction (via SVD) to the document-term matrix, yielding lower-dimensional encodings of documents as combinations of topics.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Document-Term Matrix in LSA
candidates.description: A document-term matrix is a representation where rows correspond to documents, columns to dictionary words, and cells indicate word presence or frequency.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) in LSA
candidates.description: In LSA, Singular Value Decomposition is applied to the document-term matrix to reduce its dimensionality and extract latent topics, analogous to PCA.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Text Summarization Objectives
candidates.description: Text summarization aims to condense information from one or more source texts into a shorter version that preserves the main ideas and important content, serving as a tool for accessibility and efficient information retrieval.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: Mono-document vs Multi-document Summarization
candidates.description: Summarization can be classified by the number of input documents: mono-document summarization produces a summary from a single text, while multi-document summarization synthesizes information from multiple related documents, often dealing with greater information volume.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: Extractive vs Abstractive Summarization
candidates.description: Extractive summarization selects and concatenates unchanged sentences from the source text, while abstractive summarization may rephrase or generate new sentences, potentially altering structure and meaning, and requiring more complex NLP.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: Indicative vs Informative Summaries
candidates.description: Indicative summaries provide a vague idea of the content and cannot replace the source, while informative summaries preserve the main content and can act as substitutes, allowing users to understand the subject without reading the full text.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: Generic vs User-Oriented Summaries
candidates.description: Generic summaries present the most important information without considering the user's background, while user-oriented summaries tailor the content based on the user's knowledge, providing context for novices or novelty for experts.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: Supervised vs Unsupervised Summarization
candidates.description: Supervised summarization treats sentence inclusion as a classification task trained on labeled examples, while unsupervised summarization uses pre-defined features and heuristics to determine sentence importance without needing training data.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: Intermediate Representation in Summarization
candidates.description: The first step of summarization processing is creating an intermediate representation that captures the main aspects of the text, such as topic representations using word frequency tables or more complex indicators.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: Sentence Scoring for Summarization
candidates.description: After intermediate representation, each sentence receives a score indicating its importance, often based on how well it expresses key topics or a combination of indicator evidence, sometimes using machine learning.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: Sentence Selection Algorithms
candidates.description: The summarization system selects a set of high-scoring sentences to form a summary, using greedy approaches that recalculate importance considering redundancy, or global optimization maximizing importance and coherence.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: Reformulation in Abstractive Summarization
candidates.description: In abstractive summarization, a final reformulation step rewrites or paraphrases the selected content to produce a fluent summary, often using natural language generation.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: Compression Rate in Summarization
candidates.description: Compression rate defines the size of the summary relative to the source text; e.g., a 60% compression rate means the summary will be 40% of the original length.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: Extractive Summarization Example with Python and NLTK
candidates.description: An extractive summarization workflow in Python using urllib, BeautifulSoup, NLTK for tokenization and stopword removal, then scoring sentences by word frequency to select the top sentences.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: BERT Sentence Embeddings and K-Medoid Clustering for Extractive Summarization
candidates.description: Pre-trained BERT models convert sentences into fixed-length embeddings, which are then clustered using K-medoid to select representative sentences as the extractive summary, ensuring selected sentences are actual text excerpts.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: Fine-tuning GPT-2 for Abstractive Summarization
candidates.description: GPT-2 is fine-tuned with a multi-loss strategy combining language modeling and multiple-choice prediction, using special tokens like <summarize> and keywords as input, with masked self-attention ensuring auto-regressive generation.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: Keyword Extraction for Abstractive Summarization
candidates.description: In the abstractive summarization pipeline, important keywords (nouns and verbs) are automatically extracted using techniques like NLTK POS tagging or fine-tuned BERT, providing a condensed representation for the summarization model.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: Data Scarcity in Domain-Specific Summarization
candidates.description: Low availability of domain-specific data (e.g., only 35k pairs in COVID-19 research vs 286k in general datasets) and rare terminology can hinder effective fine-tuning of large models like BERT and GPT-2.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software

candidates.label: Future Direction: Hybrid Extractive-Abstractive Summarization
candidates.description: A suggested future approach is to feed sentences extracted by extractive summarization directly into an abstractive model, potentially improving summary quality by providing richer context.
candidates.lesson_title: Sumarização de texto e Engenharia de Software
